title: Graceful Shutdown and Failure Handling
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of graceful shutdown and failure handling in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply graceful shutdown and failure handling in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to managing interrupted operations and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Graceful Shutdown and Failure Handling through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding graceful shutdown and failure handling helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Graceful Shutdown and Failure Handling helps you reason about operating-system signals. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Operating-system signals. Then connect it to Completing work safely. The remaining syllabus points—Releasing connections and resources, Managing interrupted operations—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

items.title: Assuming the happy path is enough
items.text: Test an empty value, a boundary value, and one invalid value before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Treating an example as a universal rule
items.text: Check Ruby version, runtime implementation, and third-party library documentation when behavior is version-sensitive.

items.title: Mixing too many concerns
items.text: Separate input parsing, domain behavior, and output so each piece is easier to test.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports graceful shutdown and failure handling. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for graceful shutdown and failure handling using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Managing interrupted operations), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Run, troubleshoot, and reset
content_blocks.text: Save as lesson.rb and run `ruby lesson.rb` from a terminal. CodeLeaf currently has no isolated Ruby runner, so these examples should be run locally until one is deployed. If the command fails, confirm `ruby --version`, inspect the full error message, and verify that required standard-library or gem dependencies are installed. Reset by removing temporary files created by your experiment and returning the code to the smallest reproducible example.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain graceful shutdown and failure handling, identify its place in production engineering and deployment, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
